items.q: Does deforestation only affect the trees that are cut down?
items.correct: No — it reduces biodiversity and increases atmospheric CO₂.
items.misconception: Yes, only the felled trees are affected.
items.random_wrong: It increases the amount of oxygen in the air.
items.why: Deforestation destroys habitats, lowers biodiversity, and removes trees that absorb CO₂.

items.q: Is the greenhouse effect entirely unnatural and bad?
items.correct: No — a natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth warm; the problem is the enhanced effect.
items.misconception: Yes, any greenhouse effect is harmful and man-made.
items.random_wrong: The greenhouse effect cools the planet.
items.why: Greenhouse gases naturally keep Earth habitable; extra CO₂ and methane enhance the effect, causing warming.

items.misconception: No, one species makes no difference.
items.random_wrong: It always increases the number of other species.
items.why: Each species has a role; extinctions can have wide knock-on effects on ecosystems.

items.q: Does intensive food production have downsides?
items.correct: Yes — it can harm biodiversity, soil and use large amounts of energy.
items.misconception: No, producing more food has no drawbacks.
items.random_wrong: It always improves the local environment.
items.why: Higher yields can come at an environmental cost, so there are trade-offs to manage.
